invariant: A sequence arrow is an ordered ArrowConfiguration, not a collection of unrelated booleans. CommandArrow first derives dressing1, dressing2, reverseDefine, circle decorations, body, and semantic participants from the complete arrow grammar, then applies the bracket tokens in source order. Dashed and dotted select DOTTED, hidden selects HIDDEN, bold is a no-op at the pinned revision, colors replace only color, and later tokens win. Decoration ownership follows the semantic configuration slots: reverse syntax swaps semantic participants and records reverseDefine while preserving the source circle on the sender dressing. ComponentRoseArrow always paints dressing1 then dressing2 and shortens its shaft for each attached decoration. External messages retain one of FROM_LEFT, TO_LEFT, FROM_RIGHT, or TO_RIGHT; Step1MessageExo constrains the real participant against a shared first or last border using MessageExoArrow's numbered preferred width and the live segment at the message ordinate. Autonumber formatting is resolved before label measurement, with style tags interpreted but literal angle-bracket placeholder text preserved.
causal_divergence: The first corrections fixed arrow-slot ownership, hidden autoactivation, earlier bidirectional ordering cases, one external direction, and page-end activation closure, but the AST still compresses Java's configuration too aggressively. Arrow.source_circle is recognized only when the raw token starts with `o`; reverse forms such as `A <<-o B` therefore misclassify the source circle as a target Circle head, lose elements, and reorder dressings. Open source-circle arrows pass the unshortened source coordinate to the painter even though ComponentRoseArrow advances the shaft by the circle radius, producing the observed four-pixel overrun. External rendering uses `[` and `]` sentinels, but layout reserves only FROM_LEFT and TO_RIGHT extents; FROM_RIGHT never widens the shared last border and TO_LEFT never widens the shared first border. The resulting border is then reused by the painter, so isolated and combined valid directions can be hundreds of pixels too narrow. The active-source approximation also treats depth as a scalar offset and reduces it before a following deactivation; Step1Message and MessageExoArrow instead query LifeLine's actual segment at the arrow ordinate, so an ordinary message can still depart from the deepest active Worker bar. Finally, parse_autonumber_template_runs consumes any `<...>` token as markup: `<000000>` disappears as an unknown tag and the renderer emits `1`, whereas Java preserves the angle brackets and replaces the zero run. These are model gaps, not fixture-specific geometry.
planned_change: Retain semantic decoration ownership when parsing both forward and reverse syntax: identify the target dressing independently of source-side `o`, set source_circle for `o->` and `<-o`, and keep the open or filled target head. Feed the circle-shortened endpoint to every painter branch, including open and half arrows, while preserving configuration dressing order. Keep the four external forms distinguishable through the existing side sentinels or an explicit enum, but compute one symmetric external constraint envelope: FROM_LEFT and TO_LEFT reserve the first border; FROM_RIGHT and TO_RIGHT reserve the last border; all use the formatted numbered-label width and the participant's live segment at that event. Replay activation events at message ordinates and select the deepest segment before applying a later standalone deactivation; apply inline activation or deactivation at the same ordinate according to Java event order. Teach autonumber template parsing to treat recognized style tags as markup and unrecognized numeric-placeholder angle brackets as literal text around the zero/hash run. Preserve the earlier command-admissibility dispatch, body/color ordering, hidden semantics, bidirectional dressing order, and common page-end closure. Do not special-case review labels, participant names, message counts, source coordinates, or rendered coordinates.
